notes:
### Changed

- **Agent messages: a message asks for a reply only when its sender says it needs one.** A new switch, "Ask for replies only when needed" (Settings → Agents → Agent tools, under "Let agents message each other"), is on unless you turn it off. With it on, `send_message` and `start_session` take `require_reply`: a message ends with the line asking for a reply only when the sending agent passes `require_reply: true`, and such a message carries Agent HUD's label under "Send as me" too, so the recipient knows whom to answer. Turn the switch off and every labelled message asks for a reply, as before.

### Fixes

- Agent HUD no longer keeps a processor core busy while a Grok Bot turn waits for its reply. Its data collection ran back to back for as long as the turn was open, instead of every 2 seconds at most, which showed as Agent HUD at 60–90% CPU.
- Antigravity 2.34.0: Agent HUD finds the desktop app's local service again, so its quota is read and `send_message` and `start_session` reach it. 2.34.0 stopped putting the service's token on the server's command line; Agent HUD now also reads it from the file the server saves at start. Tested on macOS (#139, thanks @JadeY001 and @cdk1025).
- An Antigravity CLI quota reading that has gone stale no longer hides the current one: once the desktop app or the IDE reads the same account, their reading is shown (#136, thanks @DDDYong).
- Linux: Agent HUD's tools and agent messages start from an installed package. `Agent HUD --mcp` answered "The installed MCP relay is missing", because the helpers a package puts under `/usr/lib` were not looked for there.
